Check or change pad assignments

Choose Learn pad, then strike it once. Repeat for rims or cymbal edges. Learning moves that note from its previous drum. Select × to ignore a note.

Pad assignments save in this browser on this device.

TD-17 USB setup and troubleshooting

Use the module’s USB COMPUTER port. For MIDI input without a Roland driver, set SETUP → USB → USB Driver Mode to GENERIC, then turn the module off and on. VENDOR also works when Roland’s Windows driver is installed. Generic mode sends pad hits, but does not send backing audio over USB.

Use Chrome on Windows or Chromebook and the HTTPS app address (or localhost). If no device appears, check the USB cable, close other music apps using the kit, then try Connect drumkit again. School browser restrictions may require an administrator.

Roland TD-17 USB settings ↗

Keyboard controls

Choose Change, then press a key. Add an alternate key for two-handed rolls. Enter starts a run; Esc stops it.

Controls saved on this device.

Drum lane order · left to right

Move each drum or cymbal to suit your kit. The hi-hat starts on the far left. This changes highway lanes, not drum notation or MIDI mappings.

Changes save automatically on this device.

Leave delay correction at 0 to start. Positive values subtract device delay from measured hits. This is a manual adjustment, not an automatic calibration.

BUILT FOR THE PRACTICE ROOM

A starting groove.

A browser prototype for Sierra Charter School. Original exercises and synthesized instrument sounds; no downloads or accounts are needed for local practice.

Built with open source

Keyboard input and control ID helpers are adapted from SightKick by Anton Korolkov, under the MIT license. MIDI file decoding uses midi-file by Carter Thaxton (MIT license). The timing engine, sounds, exercises, and interface are new.

Keyboard and shared practice

This version includes teacher/student accounts, shared school songs and saved progress when school storage is enabled. Local practice includes 24 original tracks, section repeats, drum focus, tempo building, sheet music for imported MIDI, and backing-audio sync tools. Match a beat or try a suggested alignment, then preview it before playing. USB drumkit input includes a device picker, live pad check and learnable pad assignments. Keyboard and on-screen controls stay available. The Keyboard area adds pitched MIDI practice and a note highway. Jam session lets a teacher assign two students, start a shared count-in and review separate progress and reports. Physical school-device synchronization is the next classroom trial.

Practice tips

Use wired headphones or speakers for timing practice. Some keyboards miss certain three-key combinations; change keys if a pad doesn’t light up. Touch input is useful for trying sounds; use a keyboard or USB drumkit for timing assessment.
